You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like late 2024 to early 2025. The cues:

- The policy rate is high relative to its 3-year average, but it fell over the last 3 months, which fits the Fed cutting from September 2024.
- Unemployment has risen over 3 and 12 months.
- The VIX is low and credit spreads are very tight.
- Equities and gold have done well, and gold is up sharply over 1 month.
- Headline and core CPI are low relative to their 3-year averages, as inflation has come down from the 2022 peak.
- The 10-year yield is only modestly above its average, and the 10y minus 2y spread has steepened over 12 months.
- The dollar is up 1.0 over 3 months, which fits the post-election rise in the fourth quarter of 2024.
- The equity/Treasury correlation is positive.

The strong dollar and the 1-month gold gain point to November or December 2024, but the 1-month Treasury gain of +0.5 is odd for that period. Treasuries fell in October and November 2024 and fell again in December. The 6-month Treasury return of +1.5 was strong for 7-10y bonds, from the July to September rally, so the snapshot is probably September 2024 or shortly after.

Other months fit worse. September 2024 had a 3-month dollar change that was negative, and the policy rate had not yet moved much then. Unemployment was up 12 months, which fits late 2024. The 3-month policy rate change of -1.0 means cuts of 100bp are reflected in the data, which fits December 2024 (Sep, Nov, Dec cuts). The 1-month Treasury gain fits less well, but December is the best match overall. The dollar rise and the gold spike fit a month like this, though gold fell in November 2024 and rose modestly in December.

An alternative is January 2020 or the 2019 episode. In late 2019 the Fed cut and the policy rate was high relative to its average. But unemployment then was low, and the 3-month unemployment rise doesn't fit.

I'll go with December 2024.
